    t.D23 ∧ (∀ p, ∀ o ∈ t.c1 p, w p ∈ t.c2 o) ∧

1. (`t.D23`) For every `r : R`, if there exists `o : D` such that `o` belongs to `t.c1 p'` for at least one `p' : P` (i.e., `o ∈ t.D17`) and `t.c3 o = r`, then there exist a function `S` from the set `t.D19 r = {p : P | ∃ o ∈ t.c1 p, t.c3 o = r}` to itself and an element `p` of `t.D19 r` such that the intersection `t.D20 p ∩ t.D20 (S p)` is empty, where for any `q : P`, `t.D20 q = {e : E | ∃ o ∈ t.c1 q, e ∈ t.c2 o}` (the union of `t.c2 o` over all `o ∈ t.c1 q`). Notably, both `S` and `p` are existentially quantified: `S` is only required to map that single chosen element `p` to an element `S p ∈ t.D19 r` whose `t.D20`-set is disjoint from `t.D20 p`, not to do so for all `p ∈ t.D19 r`, and no other property (such as injectivity, surjectivity, or fixed-point-freeness) is required of `S` (so this condition is logically equivalent to the existence of elements `p, q ∈ t.D19 r` with `t.D20 p ∩ t.D20 q = ∅`).

2. For every `p : P` and every `o ∈ t.c1 p`, `w p ∈ t.c2 o`. (This holds vacuously for any `p` with `t.c1 p = ∅`; when `t.c1 p` is nonempty, `w p` lies in `t.c2 o` for all `o ∈ t.c1 p`, not merely some `o`.)

3. There exist some `p : P` and some `o ∈ t.c1 p` such that `t.c4 (t.c3 o) = w p`. (This is only required for at least one such pair `(p, o)`, not for all `p` or all `o ∈ t.c1 p`, and `t.c4` is otherwise unconstrained.)

No finiteness or additional structure is required on `P`, `D`, `E`, or `R`, and none of the other definitions in the context (`S1`, `S2`, `D18`, etc.) appear in `Target`.
